name: Ceviche Clásico
description: Fresh raw fish cured in lime juice, mixed with red onion, cilantro, and ají amarillo. Peru's most iconic dish.

name: Lomo Saltado
description: Stir-fried beef tenderloin with tomatoes, onions, soy sauce, and French fries, served with white rice. A perfect blend of Peruvian and Chinese flavors.

name: Anticuchos
description: Grilled beef heart skewers marinated in vinegar, ají panca, and spices. A beloved Lima street food tradition since pre-Columbian times.

name: Causa Limeña
description: Layered cold potato dish made with ají amarillo-seasoned mashed yellow potato, filled with tuna or chicken salad and avocado.

name: Ají de Gallina
description: Shredded chicken in a creamy yellow ají amarillo sauce with bread, walnuts, and Parmesan cheese. Comfort food at its finest.
whereToTry: El Rincón que No Conoces, Lince

name: Papa a la Huancaína
description: Boiled potatoes served with a spicy, creamy sauce made from ají amarillo, fresh cheese, and crackers. A classic Peruvian starter.

name: Tiradito
description: Thinly sliced raw fish dressed with leche de tigre and ají amarillo sauce. Similar to ceviche but without onion and with Japanese Nikkei influence.

name: Arroz con Leche
description: Creamy rice pudding cooked with cinnamon, cloves, and condensed milk, topped with cinnamon powder. A classic Peruvian dessert often paired with mazamorra morada.

name: Caldo de Gallina
description: Rich hen broth with noodles, boiled egg, and vegetables. Lima's ultimate hangover cure and late-night comfort dish, served at small local restaurants.

name: Leche de Tigre
description: The citrus marinade left over from ceviche, blended with fish, ají, and cilantro. Served as a shot or small glass. Said to have energizing properties.

name: Picarones
description: Sweet potato and squash doughnuts fried and drizzled with chancaca syrup (raw cane sugar molasses). A popular street dessert during processions.

name: Seco de Res
description: Beef slow-cooked in cilantro broth with chicha de jora and vegetables, served with canary beans and white rice. Deep flavors from the north of Peru.
whereToTry: El Rincón que No Conoces, Lince

name: Chupe de Camarones
description: Hearty shrimp chowder with potatoes, corn, egg, and cheese, seasoned with ají panca. A rich and filling Peruvian soup from Arequipa.

name: Tacu Tacu
description: Leftover beans and rice pan-fried into a crispy cake, served with lomo saltado sauce or fried egg. Humble origins, extraordinary flavor.

name: Mazamorra Morada
description: Purple corn pudding cooked with dried fruits, cinnamon, cloves, and sweet potato starch. Deep purple color and sweet-spiced flavor. Lima's most beloved dessert.
